question.text:
Which of the following statements about threading models are correct?

  1. User-level threads can be implemented without modifying the operating-system kernel.
     
  2. In a pure user-level threading model, a blocking I/O operation by one thread may block all threads of the process.
     
  3. Kernel-level threads belonging to the same process cannot execute simultaneously on multiple processors.
     
  4. A hybrid threading model can map multiple user-level threads onto a smaller number of kernel scheduling entities.
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
Which of the following statements are correct?

  1. With kernel-level threads, if one thread of a process blocks, all the threads of that process will also be blocked.
     
  2. A lock implementation should always block instead of spin if it will always be used only on a uniprocessor.
     
  3. On a multiprocessor, a lock implementation should spin instead of block if it is known that the lock will be available before the time required for a context switch.
     
  4. Periodically yielding the processor while spin-waiting reduces the amount of wasted time to be proportional to the duration of a time slice.
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
Which of the following statements about context switching are correct?

  1. When switching between two threads, the registers, stack pointer, and program counter of the outgoing thread must be saved.
     
  2. Switching between two threads of the same process always requires loading a different top-level page-table pointer.
     
  3. When switching between threads belonging to different processes, the address-space information of the incoming process must be loaded.
     
  4. A thread cannot be context-switched while it is executing inside a critical section and holding a lock.
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
Which of the following statements are correct?

  1. Threads belonging to the same process use a common stack.
     
  2. Threads belonging to the same process can use the same valid TLB entries.
     
  3. Multiple kernel-level threads of the same process may execute simultaneously on different CPUs.
     
  4. Holding a lock prevents the operating-system scheduler from context-switching the thread.
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
Which of the following statements are correct?

  1. Threads that are part of the same process share the same stack pointer.
     
  2. Threads that are part of the same process share the same page-table base register.
     
  3. Threads that are part of the same process share the same general-purpose registers.
     
  4. Context-switching between threads of the same process requires flushing the TLB or tracking an ASID in the TLB.
question.subject: Operating System
